title: Tencent Hy3: A 295B Open MoE Model Under Apache 2.0
hook: Tencent's new Hy3 model switched from a restrictive community license to Apache 2.0 — removing the regional-use carve-outs that blocked adoption in the EU, UK, and South Korea.
key_points: Hy3: 295B total parameters, 21B active per token — a sparse mixture-of-experts model from Tencent.
License changed from a restrictive community license (which barred use in South Korea, the UK, and EU) to Apache 2.0 for the non-preview release.
Follows a pattern of major Chinese labs relaxing licensing terms on open-weight releases to broaden international adoption.
Early local-inference reports describe it as competitive with DeepSeek-V4 Flash despite the meaningfully smaller size, and runnable on a 128GB MacBook.
content_html: Open-weight model releases from major labs increasingly come with a catch: a "community" license with regional carve-outs that quietly excludes some of the biggest markets. Tencent's Hy3 is notable for dropping that catch.
extra_html:
Hy3 is a 295B-total, 21B-active-parameter sparse mixture-of-experts model. Its preview release carried a restrictive community license that barred use in South Korea, the UK, and the EU; the non-preview release switched to Apache 2.0, removing those restrictions entirely. It's part of a broader pattern of major Chinese AI labs loosening licensing terms on open-weight releases specifically to widen international adoption — a trend worth watching alongside the raw model capabilities themselves. Reported on r/LocalLLaMA, 2026-07-06.

A follow-up local-inference report (r/LocalLLaMA, 2026-07-10) adds a capability angle: after running Hy3 on a 128GB MacBook M5 Max, the poster described it as competitive with DeepSeek-V4 Flash while being meaningfully smaller — notable given DeepSeek-V4 Flash itself already needs specialized handling to run well locally (see the DSA-indexer patch card). Take single-user impressions like this as anecdotal until broader benchmarks land.

related.title: LongCat 2.0: A 1.6T-Parameter Open Model Under MIT License
related.hook: 1.6 trillion total parameters, ~48B active, and released under the MIT license — one of the most permissively licensed large open-weight MoE models yet.

related.title: What Is a Mixture of Experts?
related.hook: Instead of running every input through one big network, route each token to a few specialist sub-networks - total capacity grows without proportional compute.

related.title: Kimi K2: Open Agentic Intelligence
related.hook: Moonshot's Kimi K2 is a trillion-parameter open-weight Mixture-of-Experts model built agentic-first — and trained at that scale without a single loss spike using the MuonClip optimizer.

related.title: DeepSeek-V4: Sparse Attention, Million-Token Default
related.hook: DeepSeek-V4 makes a 1M-token context window the default and pairs token-wise compression with sparse attention, so long-context inference no longer pays the usual compute and memory tax.

flashcards.prompt: What changed between Hy3's preview and non-preview release?
flashcards.back_html: The license switched from a restrictive community license — which barred use in South Korea, the UK, and the EU — to the permissive Apache 2.0 license.

flashcards.explanation_html: Hy3 is a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 295B total parameters and 21B active per token — in the same broad open-MoE class as other recent releases like LongCat 2.0, but roughly a fifth the total size.

flashcards.prompt: How does Hy3 compare to DeepSeek-V4 Flash according to early local-inference reports?
flashcards.back_html: Reports describe Hy3 as competitive with DeepSeek-V4 Flash despite being meaningfully smaller, and practical to run locally on a 128GB MacBook.
